A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UCAT research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial reformatting and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original robustness and uncertainty experiments on 16 single-label datasets and MS-COCO, with ablations and additional training, attack, and backbone evaluations in its appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds comparator results, forward-KL ablations, and expanded multi-label adversarial evaluations.

M1.justification: The evidence mapping and UCAT objective remain unchanged: text-guided cross-entropy plus KL(Dir(alpha_adv) || Dir(alpha)), with the same encoder arrangement. v2 explicitly calls this reverse KL and explains its motivation; it does not introduce that direction as a new method component.

E1.justification: The datasets and recognition tasks are retained. MS-COCO test conditions expand from one reported CW adversarial comparison to clean evaluation and CW/PGD perturbations through 4/255, including joint all-label PGD (v2 Tables 1 and 5). ImageNet-scale training and CLIP/SLIP backbone evaluations already existed in v1.

E2.justification: Comp-TGA (Yu et al., 2026) joins the evaluated comparators in the COCO and TinyImageNet-trained single-label comparisons. The earlier ZSAR comparators remain, as do the appendix comparisons with TRADES, ACAT, and DKL.

E3.justification: v2 Appendix A changes the reported strong-training PGD step size from 2/255 to 1/255 and fixes evaluation PGD steps at 1/255 instead of epsilon. COCO Table 1 changes the stated training radius from 2/255 to 1/255, expands attack radii and clean evaluation, and replaces top-5 metrics with H(F1@3). Appendix D.1 adds PGD-100 maximizing all-label BCE. These are documented protocol changes; the PDFs do not establish which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 Table 4 extends v1 Table 3 with forward softmax-KL and forward Dirichlet-KL controls, directly testing divergence direction alongside distribution level. It also adds joint-PGD and attack-budget analyses on COCO and uncertainty CDFs for CIFAR-10. The temperature and backbone studies already present in v1's appendices should not be counted as new analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Expanded predictive-uncertainty plots describe model behavior rather than introducing statistical uncertainty estimates for experimental results.

E6.justification: v2 adds Comp-TGA, expanded COCO, joint-PGD, and forward-KL results, while removing COCO top-5 scores. The new forward-Dirichlet ablation reports 24.36 AutoAttack accuracy versus 30.58 for the retained reverse direction. PMG-AFT's strong-setting AutoAttack average changes from 0.25 to 2.06 (v1 Table 5; v2 Table 6), and backbone harmonic means are revised. All pre-existing rows in main Table 2 remain numerically unchanged. Protocol edits prevent interpreting replaced values uniformly as same-setting gains.

T1.justification: The Dirichlet definition, concentration bounds, monotonicity, softmax equivalence, invariance corollary, and proofs are retained after renumbering (v1 Appendix D; v2 Appendix B). Equivalent InfoNCE notation and explicit l-infinity PGD notation clarify existing mathematics without changing the theoretical argument.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: adversarial uncertainty suppression, a Dirichlet interpretation of CLIP, and distributional alignment improving calibration while balancing robustness and clean accuracy. Added evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds a mode-seeking explanation for reverse KL and reframes the COCO interpretation around top-ranked reliability versus global mAP ordering. Section 4 narrows the assertion that CLIP implicitly optimizes a Dirichlet model to a Dirichlet-consistent reinterpretation. Meanwhile, v1 Appendix G's explicit discussion of image-only attacks, fine-tuning requirements, test-time defenses, and broader applicability is removed.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link in Section 6 and specifies BCEWithLogitsLoss over all target labels for the new COCO attack. It also revises documented PGD step sizes. Batch size, training epochs, temperature choices, and AU/EU computation details are otherwise retained; repository availability was not externally verified.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially recast around closed-set versus open-vocabulary robustness, prompt tuning, test-time defenses, and logit-scale calibration, with new citations including Dong et al., LeVine et al., Murugesan et al., and Comp-TGA. v2 acknowledges earlier softmax-distribution alignment and drops the blanket first-theoretical-account assertion. Much of v1's extended contrastive-learning and uncertainty background is removed.

P1.justification: v2 extensively rewrites related work and experimental interpretation, introduces a main-text backbone subsection, and reorganizes the appendices. The separate extended-related-work, LLM-disclosure, and limitations sections disappear; impact and acknowledgment sections replace earlier front/back-matter arrangements. These are substantial narrative and structural revisions.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column layout. Figure 1 gains CDF panels, while its previous uncertainty bars move to appendix Figure 5; AU/EU plots are redrawn with annotations. Figure 3 adds a temperature panel, and a backbone summary table redisplays appendix results. COCO tables expand, the ablation table gains rows, and the former strong-attack tables are merged.

improvement.justification: The added KL-direction controls and broader COCO evaluation strengthen support for the existing method, while updated positioning and a code link improve usefulness. These are incremental gains over an already extensive v1. They are offset by removal of explicit limitations and reporting problems: attack-setting descriptions remain difficult to reconcile, and v2 changes CLIP-B/16's harmonic mean from 38.73 to 39.05 despite retaining clean/robust means of 52.91 and 30.54, which imply approximately 38.73.
